items.fullText: 테크 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 김진욱 마인드로직 대표 "챗GPT·클로드 한곳에…AI 구독시장 바꿀 것" 입력 2026.10.30 09:59 수정 2026.10.30 10:07 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 유지희 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 챗GPT·클로드 등 AI 80개 모델 한곳에 대학 고객 1년 새 28곳서 100곳으로 초·중·고교 등 포함 고객 기관 600곳 돌파 이수만도 투자…AI 팬 소통 서비스 개발 김진욱 마인드로직 공동대표가 28일 한국경제신문과 인터뷰하고 있다. 사진=피알브릿지 제공 “알뜰폰이라고 통화가 안 되는 건 아니잖아요. 인공지능(AI)도 비싼 구독료를 매달 내는 대신 필요한 만큼 골라 쓰면 됩니다.” 김진욱 마인드로직 공동대표는 30일 한국경제신문과의 인터뷰에서 AI 구독료 부담을 낮추겠다는 사업 구상을 이같이 설명했다. 김 대표는 글로벌 컨설팅 기업 맥킨지에서 함께 근무했던 김용우 공동대표와 2019년 마인드로직을 창업했다. 이 회사는 챗GPT·클로드·제미나이 등 80여 개 AI 모델을 한곳에서 이용할 수 있는 통합 플랫폼을 운영한다. 대학과 공공기관, 기업 등에 서비스를 공급하고 있다. 마인드로직은 지난해부터 대학을 대상으로 생성형 AI 통합 서비스 ‘베이즈 엔터프라이즈(팩트챗)’를 공급하며 빠르게 성장했다. 김 대표는 “서비스를 도입한 대학이 지난해 10월 28곳에서 올해 100곳으로 늘었다”며 초·중·고교와 공공기관, 기업까지 포함하면 도입 기관이 600곳을 넘는다”고 말했다. 지난 15일에는 월 5900원에 이용할 수 있는 일반 소비자용 플랫폼 ‘베이즈’도 출시했다. 대학에서 서비스를 이용하던 졸업생들의 요청이 계기가 됐다. 그는 “학교에서 서비스를 이용하던 졸업생들이 사회에 나와서도 계속 쓰고 싶다는 의견을 전해왔다”고 설명했다. 저렴한 AI 서비스의 필요성에 주목한 계기는 대학생들의 이용 실태였다. 김 대표는 “대학생 네 명이 챗GPT 계정 하나를 함께 쓰고, 여덟 명이 공유하는 경우도 있다고 하더라”며 “2024년 한 대학이 AI 대화 서비스 이용료로 월 3500만원을 지출하는 것을 보고 비용 절감의 필요성을 느꼈다”고 말했다. 김진욱 마인드로직 공동대표가 28일 한국경제신문과 인터뷰하고 있다. 사진=피알브릿지 제공 마인드로직의 차별점은 AI 모델을 바꾸더라도 이용자와의 대화 맥락을 이어갈 수 있다는 것이다. 베이즈에서 챗GPT를 이용하다 클로드로 바꾸더라도 이전 대화 정보를 활용할 수 있다. 시스템 프롬프트 최적화와 캐싱, 자체 임베딩 기술 등을 통해 토큰 사용량도 줄인다. 김 대표는 “API 방식으로 여러 AI 모델을 한곳에 모아놓는 것은 어려운 일이 아니다”며 “중요한 것은 좋은 답변을 더 적은 비용으로 제공하는 기술”이라고 강조했다. 대화형 AI 기술은 엔터테인먼트 분야로도 활용 범위를 넓히고 있다. 지난 14일 A2O엔터테인먼트가 선보인 신인 걸그룹 ‘A2O 라이트’의 AI 팬 소통 서비스 ‘블루밍톡’에 마인드로직의 기술이 적용됐다. A2O엔터테인먼트의 이수만 키 프로듀서(전 SM엔터테인먼트 총괄 프로듀서)는 2024년 마인드로직에 70억원을 투자했다. 오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등 주요 AI 개발사들이 자체 서비스를 운영하는 만큼 사업 확장에 한계가 있을 수 있다는 우려도 제기된다. 이에 김 대표는 유통 플랫폼에 비유해 차별성을 강조했다. 그는 “화장품 제조사에 올리브영이나 다이소가 중요한 유통 파트너인 것처럼 우

items.t: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT
items.d: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings is buying ADT in a $15.3 billion deal, with plans to bring AI to the home security business.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 12:56 PM PDT · October 29, 2026 Image Credits: Timon Schneider/SOPA Images/LightRocket / Getty Images Julie Bort OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT Thrive Holdings has acquired physical security company ADT for $10 per share or about $7.6 billion in equity, the companies announced on Thursday. Beyond equity, the total enterprise value of the deal is $15.3 billion, ADT said. Thrive Holdings is the holding company spinout from Josh Kushner’s powerhouse VC firm Thrive Capital. It also counts OpenAI as its partner , as well as an investor. The firm’s mission is to hold other companies long-term, revitalizing them with AI. Currently, Thrive Holdings holds over 75 companies, it says. As a partner, OpenAI supplies AI models and tech as well as people, otherwise known as forward-deployed engineers, to Thrive’s companies. Neither ADT nor Thrive announced what new AI-powered security products they will be releasing, but they did tease that the plan was to invest and release new products. “ADT will form the foundation of Thrive Holdings’ smart home security business,” the press release said. AI-powered physical security is having a moment right now. Apple just entered the field with a new line of smart home and home security products in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. Amazon updated its smart home line, including new AI-powered home cameras . ADT already partners with Apple and Google and is expected to continue to do so. And who knows what the future might bring? Some startups are offering AI dog robots as roving security guards . Note: This story was updated to include ADT’s current partnerships and to describe Thrive Holdings as a holding company. items.t: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction
items.d: Dream is grounded in real physics and construction standards. Just as LLMs learn from text, Dream's world model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data gathered from permit archives across the United States.
items.fullText: Andy Elder and Arjun Mathur were Stanford roommates who both studied computer science before spending a decade at Palantir. Elder led product design for a team of 800 people building software for U.S. defense and intelligence agencies, while Mathur served as a senior vice president in the company’s commercial practice. When the friends decided to build a startup early last year, there was no question they would do it together. Despite having no direct background in architecture, Elder and Mathur were troubled by a growing problem: Fewer buildings are constructed in the U.S. today than a few decades ago , as development costs have surged. “We’ve gone from dial-up internet to superintelligent AI, but our ability to build the physical world around us has actually decreased,” Mathur told TechCrunch. Believing AI can boost productivity across the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, they set out to build Dream , a startup developing built world models that automate building design and engineering. Dream has emerged from stealth with $17 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, alongside other backers, including SV Angel, XYZ, and Zigg Capital. The startup aims to replace cumbersome, outdated AEC tools like Autodesk’s AutoCAD and Revit. If you sit next to an architect or a structural engineer, you’ll notice that they are still “drawing” every piece of their designs part by part on legacy software, Mathur said. “AI really plays no role in that equation.” While a standard LLM like ChatGPT can generate an image of a building, the result won’t be structurally sound. Dream, by contrast, is grounded in real physics and construction standards. Just as LLMs learn from text, Dream’s world model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data gathered from permit archives across the United States. “Our model actually understands what’s within those walls. October 29, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Create an Editable Building Model From Site Scans 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/relay-video-v14-1080p.mp4 Planning warehouse automation requires a model of the building itself, but shelving and machinery can obscure its structure in site scans. Omniverse brings together real-to-sim tools and agent skills to help developers turn real-world captures into editable starting environments for physical AI simulation. David Wehr, from NVIDIA’s simulation technology team, built on that work using Astra to develop a workflow for digitally reconstructing a building without its contents. The goal is an editable, simulation-ready building model where developers can add or reposition shelving and machinery to evaluate warehouse layouts and automation plans before making physical changes. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Anthropic reveals $80 billion loss, huge spending spree ahead of IPO The company warned that AI could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” as cybersecurity fears grow. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 AI startup Anthropic unveils its public IPO filing for the first time 03:17 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 26, 2026, 9:12 AM EDT / Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 11:16 AM EDT By Steve Kopack Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic on Monday unveiled its public IPO filing ahead of what is expected to be one of the largest stock debuts in history. That offering, widely expected to come sometime in mid-November, could value the Claude developer at more than $2 trillion. That could surpass the current record holder, Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in an IPO in June that valued the rocket-AI-social-media firm at $2.1 trillion. The filing did not include a potential share price, the number of shares to be offered or a valuation for the whole company, all of which will be determined after Anthropic holds a “road show” with investors, prospective investors and its bankers. Monday’s filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission showed that Anthropic, like other AI firms, is splashing out unprecedented amounts of cash on cloud services to run its AI models. The company plans to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon for cloud services through April 2036 and another $120 billion with SpaceX through 2029. Anthropic also said it planned to spend $115 billion with Google and $45 billion with Microsoft, both through 2033, for computing infrastructure. The filing said that the company recorded revenue growth of “1,368% year over year for the three months ended June 30, 2026.” The cost of renting servers and chips grew by 300% over the same period. items.fullText: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations October 21, 2026 by Mavi Nafria 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. items.fullText: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents Growing ecosystem of AI clouds across Europe, Nordics, Africa and Central Asia build full-stack NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factories as AI-native companies drive demand for sovereign compute, training, inference and post-training services. October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements.
